exposure: attendance at a specialist preterm surveillance clinic (PSC)
previous full dilatation caesarean section birth
cohort: 762 asymptomatic high-risk pregnant women who attended a specialist preterm surveillance clinic (PSC) in Ireland between January 2019 and December 2022
finding: Over 80% of women considered high risk for preterm birth delivered at term after attending a PSC, suggesting that serial cervical surveillance can help identify those who would benefit most from interventions.
mod_finding: Women who delivered before 37 weeks were significantly more likely to have had a previous full-dilation Cesarean section birth.
gest_age: Median gestational age at birth: 38.6 weeks (IQR 37.2-39.6 weeks)
birth_weight: Median birthweight for infants born before 37 weeks: 2270 g, Median birthweight for infants born at term: 3300 g
